subject: general
question: The Postal Index Number (PIN) is a six digit code used by Indian postal department, what does the first two digit of the code (taken together) stands for:

options.text: Sub region or one of the postal circles

solution:
The correct answer is __**Sub region or one of the postal circles**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first two digits of the Postal Index Number (PIN) in India represent a **sub region or one of the postal circles**.
 
• India is divided into nine PIN zones, including one for the Indian Army.
 
• Each postal circle is assigned a unique range of PIN codes, which helps in efficiently sorting and delivering mail.
 
• The system was introduced on 15 August 1972 by Shriram Bhikaji Velankar, an additional secretary in the Union Ministry of Communications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The PIN system is essential for ensuring the speedy and accurate delivery of mail across India.
 
• Each digit in the PIN code has a specific significance, with the first digit representing the zone, the second digit representing the sub-region, and the third digit representing the sorting district.
 
• The remaining three digits are assigned to individual post offices within the sorting district.
 
• The introduction of the PIN system has greatly improved the efficiency and reliability of the Indian postal service.
